newsitem.title: GREECE: Stronger drachma likely in near-term -- Citibank.
newsitem.headline: Stronger drachma likely in near-term -- Citibank.

text.p: The Greek drachma is likely to continue to appreciate in the near term because of foreign inflows to "lock into" relatively high yields on state debt, Citibank, London, said in its November report.
"Unhurried easing will continue to attract investors, especially since inflation remains problematic," it said.
It also cited planned privatisations as another factor which could lead to more direct investment and further strengthen the drachma.

As a result, it said "Notwithstanding our bearish fundamental outlook on the Greek currency because of the external position, it is entirely possible that an unsustainable burst of appreciation could be in the offing in the near-term."
Greece's European Union convergence programme rules out fiscal laxity and some monetary easing is required to discourage capital inflows, it said.
"This too could attract a rush of foreign capital to lock in rates," the report added.
Thus an unsustainable appreciation of the drachma could be in the offing in the short-run even if the Greek authorities cut interest rates, it said.
Greece's key 12-month T-bill yield was at 12.30 percent and inflation was at 8.3 percent year-on-year in October. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
